error.signature: AI assumes getting a Danish MitID digital ID (via passport, without a CPR number) grants access to online or mobile banking

verdict.summary: Non-citizens without a Danish CPR number can get MitID (Denmark's national digital ID) using an 8-digit P-code tied to a foreign passport instead. However, MitID's own help pages and Danish banks (e.g. Danske Bank) state that most self-service solutions, including eBanking and Mobile Bank, currently require a MitID created with a genuine CPR number or civil registration number at 'Substantial' security level - a P-code MitID cannot log into online or mobile banking.

dead_ends.action: Get a P-code MitID with a foreign passport and expect it to work for Danish online or mobile banking
dead_ends.why_fails: MitID's official help page for non-citizens states 'most self-service solutions currently require a CPR number. It's not possible to access these self-service solutions with a MitID created with a P code.' Danske Bank confirms a MitID must be created with a valid CPR number or civil registration number, at the 'Substantial' security level, to log into eBanking and Mobile Bank.
dead_ends.condition: MitID created via P-code, no CPR number yet

workarounds.action: Obtain a Danish CPR number first (see the CPR-registration canon for this country), then create or upgrade MitID using the CPR number so it reaches the 'Substantial' security level required for eBanking and Mobile Bank
workarounds.how: Danske Bank directs customers without a CPR number to obtain one via the official Danish civil registration channel before MitID can be used for banking.
workarounds.condition: Newcomer who has not yet registered for a CPR number

workarounds.action: For the interim, contact the bank directly for a branch-based or paper-based process instead of relying on MitID-gated self-service
workarounds.condition: Urgent banking need before CPR number is issued
workarounds.tradeoff: Slower and may require an in-person branch visit each time.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: This canon covers what MitID access level is possible without CPR; the other covers the CPR-registration process itself.
